forces.title: High financing costs and geopolitical risks cap residential growth
forces.description: Europe's construction sector, including residential, faces subdued growth due to persistently high financing costs and escalating geopolitical risks, particularly the conflict in the Middle East. These factors deter both households and businesses from investing in new properties, with buyers reluctant to commit to new builds that have long completion times amid uncertainty. This economic environment is capping momentum and delaying a stronger residential recovery across the EU.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Residential building sector remains weak due to rates and costs
forces.description: The building sector, encompassing both residential and non-residential construction, is identified as a weak spot across Europe. This is primarily driven by higher interest rates, which increase financing burdens for buyers and developers, and elevated construction costs. Combined with general economic uncertainty, these factors lead to increased caution among households and businesses regarding new property investments, slowing down activity in the residential market.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Higher interest rates reduce new home affordability for buyers
forces.description: Elevated interest rates are significantly impacting the affordability of new homes, making them less accessible for buyers across Europe. This is particularly challenging for new builds, as buyers often need to finance payments during the construction period, amplifying the effect of higher rates. The increased cost of borrowing consequently reduces overall demand for new residential properties, contributing to stalled growth in the sector.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Rising energy prices increase building material costs and developer burden
forces.description: Higher energy prices are pushing up production costs for energy-intensive building materials such as concrete, cement, and bricks, impacting residential construction across Europe. Although the overall rise in construction costs has been modest, passing these increased input costs through the value chain to buyers is becoming increasingly difficult. This leaves many new-build projects unprofitable, especially in markets where existing homes are comparatively cheaper, forcing developers to postpone construction.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: France's zero-interest mortgage scheme yet to boost housing construction
forces.description: France expanded its zero-interest mortgage scheme (PTZ) for new-build homes in April 2025, aiming to support first-time buyers and stimulate housing construction. However, recent building permit data suggests that this policy has not yet gained significant traction, as permits remained below previous year levels. The scheme's intended positive impact on residential development is currently limited, failing to offset broader headwinds in the sector.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Dutch grid congestion and nitrogen restrictions delay construction projects
forces.description: In the Netherlands, limited grid capacity continues to delay new connections for construction projects, particularly impacting residential development. Furthermore, ongoing nitrogen restrictions cause additional setbacks, hindering the progress of permitted housing projects. These execution constraints are significant headwinds, leading to an increasing number of permitted homes awaiting the start of construction, and limiting the translation of permits into actual housing completions.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Developer profitability squeezed by inability to pass on high costs
forces.description: Residential developers in countries like France, Germany, and Austria face severe profitability challenges as they are unable to fully pass on higher material costs to buyers. Existing-home prices in these markets have risen less than the European average, and in France, they remain below levels from three years ago. This disparity means new-build projects often become unprofitable at current market prices, forcing developers to postpone construction until conditions become more favorable for cost recovery.
forces.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

forces.title: Weak mortgage lending and higher rates curb Belgian housing demand
forces.description: Mortgage lending in Belgium remains weak, with the number of new mortgages falling by approximately 10% in the first eight months of 2026 compared to the previous year. This decline, combined with continuously rising long-term interest rates and mortgage rates influenced by geopolitical tensions, significantly reduces housing affordability and buyer borrowing capacity. The weak mortgage activity is a strong headwind that suggests a slowdown in housing market momentum in the coming quarters.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Energy efficiency premium widens for Belgian homes amid higher prices
forces.description: The current environment of higher energy prices is expected to further widen the price gap between energy-efficient and energy-intensive homes in Belgium. As energy consumption rises, the financial benefits of efficient housing become more visible, reinforcing a trend seen since the 2022 energy crisis. Energy performance is now an increasingly critical determinant of property value and marketability, acting as a hedge against future energy price shocks and regulatory risks, thereby driving structural demand for sustainable properties.
forces.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

forces.title: Increased housing supply boosts sales but moderates price growth
forces.description: The Dutch housing market is experiencing a significant increase in available homes for sale, including a substantial flow of former rental properties from investors. This growing supply is boosting existing home transactions towards record highs by easing previous supply constraints and improving market mobility. However, this increased supply, coupled with higher mortgage rates and weaker consumer sentiment, is simultaneously reducing upward pressure on house prices, leading to more moderate growth.
forces.source_title: More Dutch housing supply pushes transactions to record highs

forces.title: Rising household incomes and first-time buyer support bolster demand
forces.description: Household incomes in the Netherlands continue to rise, with wage growth expected to remain above average at around 3% year-on-year through the end of next year. This income growth provides crucial support for house prices. Additionally, first-time buyers are increasingly contributing more of their own funds and receiving growing financial support through municipal loans, easing their entry into the market and further underpinning demand for owner-occupied homes.
forces.source_title: More Dutch housing supply pushes transactions to record highs

forces.title: Irish housing investment constrained by taxation and rent-cap policies
forces.description: Ireland's housing sector is facing significant headwinds from specific government policies, including taxation and rent-cap regulations. These measures have constrained investment in residential development across certain areas, despite strong underlying demand. The policies reduce the attractiveness and viability of new housing projects for developers and investors, contributing to the housing segment being the weakest performer within the broader construction sector and hindering supply growth.
forces.source_title: July 2026 Ireland Sector Snippets

forces.title: Residential rent regulation and tax changes weigh on investor interest
forces.description: The introduction of residential rent regulation in 2024 and significant increases in transfer tax (from 2% in 2020 to 10.4% in 2025, then 8% for residential in 2026) have fundamentally reshaped the Dutch residential investment landscape. These policy changes, combined with higher interest rates, have weighed heavily on investor interest, particularly from foreign entities who have largely exited the market. This structural shift makes selling existing rental properties more attractive than continued leasing.
forces.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

forces.title: AI adoption to transform housing value chain and efficiency
forces.description: Artificial Intelligence is poised to transform the residential real estate sector globally, with the potential to unlock significant annual value. AI is changing how consumers discover, compare, and engage with housing, as well as enhancing operational efficiency in design, scheduling, and construction. Key opportunities include streamlining lead-to-appointment processes, improving affordability assessments, optimizing pricing and incentives, and making maintenance more responsive. This represents a structural change in industry operations and customer experience.
forces.source_title: ...value creation in residential real estate.

forces.title: Lack of transparency in HOA sustainability efforts deters investment
forces.description: In the Netherlands, efforts by Homeowners' Associations (HOAs) to prepare for sustainable renovations are largely invisible to prospective buyers. This lack of transparency means the value added by such preparations is rarely reflected in property prices, thereby weakening incentives for HOAs to invest time and effort in these measures. Buyers struggle to assess HOA progress due to inaccessible or difficult-to-interpret documents, causing them to perceive HOA contributions as costs rather than investments, which postpones collective sustainability actions.
forces.source_title: The hidden value of sustainability efforts in Dutch HOAs

forces.title: High approval thresholds and diverse interests hinder HOA renovations
forces.description: Collective sustainability measures in Dutch Homeowners' Associations (HOAs) require high approval thresholds, typically two-thirds to three-quarters of members, making it difficult to gain sufficient support. This challenge is compounded by financially constrained households within HOAs, often with lower reserves and incomes in less energy-efficient buildings. Diverging interests between landlords and owner-occupiers, and varying financial benefits among residents, further complicate decision-making, significantly slowing the pace of necessary renovations.
forces.source_title: The hidden value of sustainability efforts in Dutch HOAs

forces.title: Government plans to lower HOA renovation approval threshold
forces.description: To accelerate the sustainability of HOA apartments, the Dutch government is planning to lower the approval threshold for collective sustainability plans to 50% + 1 in 2027, down from the current two-thirds to three-quarters. This policy change is expected to make decision-making easier within Homeowners' Associations, potentially overcoming one of the key barriers to initiating much-needed renovation measures. This is a significant tailwind aimed at stimulating investment in energy efficiency across a substantial portion of the housing stock.
forces.source_title: The hidden value of sustainability efforts in Dutch HOAs

forces.title: Short-term rentals reduce housing supply in key Belgian cities
forces.description: Short-term rental platforms, such as Airbnb, are reducing the available housing supply in Belgium's high-demand urban and tourist areas, adding pressure to already tight housing markets. An estimated 5,000 homes in Brussels, Antwerp, and Ghent combined are effectively removed from the regular housing stock, representing approximately 0.8% of the rental market. While new European regulations aim to address this by requiring data sharing, the direct impact on housing affordability remains a notable headwind.
forces.source_title: Airbnb only part of Belgium’s housing affordability problem

forces.title: Declining homeownership and rising renters pressure rental markets
forces.description: Belgium is experiencing a structural shift in its housing market, with the homeownership rate declining from 72.4% in 2022 to 70.9% in 2025. This trend is accompanied by a growing number of renters, which intensifies pressure on already tight rental markets. This fundamental change in housing tenure contributes to affordability challenges and highlights a systemic need for increased and appropriately matched rental housing supply to meet evolving demographic and economic demands.
forces.source_title: Airbnb only part of Belgium’s housing affordability problem

forces.title: Low construction activity and supply-demand mismatch hinder affordability
forces.description: Belgium faces persistent housing affordability challenges due to historically low construction activity, with building permits remaining at subdued levels despite recent upticks. Furthermore, there's a significant mismatch between new construction and demand, as apartment permits are declining (-8% YoY) despite rising demand for smaller units, while single-family home permits are increasing (+17% YoY). This misaligned supply exacerbates housing tightness and affordability issues, especially in urban rental markets.
forces.source_title: Airbnb only part of Belgium’s housing affordability problem

forces.title: Tightened housing regulation and rent caps constrain rental supply
forces.description: Belgium's housing market is impacted by significantly tightened housing regulations, including rent caps, which aim to serve legitimate objectives but carry unintended consequences. Evidence suggests these measures can reduce rental supply, dampen new construction, and lower overall market turnover. This regulatory framework, while well-intentioned, acts as a headwind for developers and investors in the residential rental sector, potentially exacerbating supply shortages and making housing affordability more challenging.
forces.source_title: Airbnb only part of Belgium’s housing affordability problem

viewpoints.title: European residential construction recovery delayed by stabilized housing permits
viewpoints.description: ING Research expects Europe's residential construction recovery to be delayed, with growth remaining modest. Housing permits have stabilized, indicating that a stronger rebound is not imminent. This stabilization, coupled with higher financing costs and ongoing geopolitical risks, is capping momentum in the sector, despite some broader economic resilience. The building sector, which includes residential construction, continues to be a weak spot, hindering overall growth.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: German housing construction poised for modest recovery in 2026-2027
viewpoints.description: Germany's construction sector, after five years of contraction (over 10% decline between 2020 and 2025), is anticipated to return to modest growth in 2026. This recovery is expected to gain momentum in 2027, supported by renewed activity in both housing and infrastructure projects. Despite this positive outlook, the impact of government initiatives like 'housing construction turbo' on speeding up planning and approvals remains dependent on local authorities.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: French housing permits fall, signalling 2.5% construction contraction
viewpoints.description: French housing permits in August 2026 remained below the previous year's levels, despite early promising data. This, combined with sluggish GDP growth, points to an expected 2.5% contraction in the French construction sector for 2026. Efforts to boost housing construction, such as expanding the zero-interest mortgage scheme for new-build homes, have not yet gained sufficient traction to reverse the downward trend.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Dutch housing recovery limited despite increased permits and stabilizing output
viewpoints.description: Dutch construction output is expected to stabilize in 2026 after a weak first half, with modest growth anticipated in 2027. Housing construction should gradually recover as a recent surge in building permits translates into starts and completions. However, the recovery remains limited due to project delays, grid capacity constraints, and nitrogen restrictions. These factors collectively temper the positive signals from permit issuance, suggesting a prolonged and gradual rebound.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: New housing projects struggle commercially amid high costs and competition
viewpoints.description: Despite severe housing shortages in many European cities, new housing projects face significant commercial viability challenges. High construction costs cannot be fully passed on to buyers, especially in markets where existing homes remain cheaper than new builds. This price differential pushes many buyers towards existing properties, leaving new projects unprofitable at current market prices. Consequently, developers are postponing construction until market conditions improve.
viewpoints.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

viewpoints.title: Belgian building permit recovery remains fragile despite initial growth
viewpoints.description: After a period of decline, Belgian building permits saw a welcome 8% increase in the first half of 2026, driven by new residential construction. However, permit volumes remain historically low, and renewed geopolitical tensions are adding new headwinds. Rising energy and material costs are pushing up new home prices, while increasing interest and mortgage rates reduce housing affordability. This combination of factors is dampening demand and weakening order books, indicating a fragile recovery.
viewpoints.source_title: Belgian building permit recovery continues, but challenges lie ahead

viewpoints.title: Belgian housing market resilience masks a challenging outlook ahead
viewpoints.description: The Belgian housing market demonstrated unexpected resilience in Q2 2026, with modest price increases and transaction recovery. However, this masks a challenging outlook. Weak mortgage lending, persistently high interest rates, and renewed geopolitical tensions suggest that demand will lose momentum. Furthermore, rising energy prices are expected to widen the value gap for energy-efficient homes, making property value increasingly dependent on energy performance.
viewpoints.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

viewpoints.title: Increased Dutch housing supply drives record sales, moderating price growth
viewpoints.description: The growing supply of homes in the Netherlands, including a substantial share from investors selling rental properties, is pushing existing home sales toward record highs in 2026. This increased market mobility and easing of supply constraints are boosting transactions. Concurrently, larger supply combined with higher mortgage rates and weaker sentiment is reducing upward pressure on house prices, which are expected to rise at a more moderate pace, ending 2026 around 3% higher.
viewpoints.source_title: More Dutch housing supply pushes transactions to record highs

viewpoints.title: Irish housing remains weakest construction segment despite strong underlying demand
viewpoints.description: In Ireland, housing continues to be the weakest-performing segment within the broader construction sector. This underperformance is attributed to taxation and rent-cap policies, which have constrained investment in residential development in certain areas. Despite these policy-induced limitations on investment, the underlying demand for housing remains strong. This robust demand is expected to support activity in the longer term, assuming policy adjustments or market adaptations can mitigate current investment barriers.

viewpoints.title: Investment in affordable rental housing in Netherlands limited by weak viability
viewpoints.description: The growth potential for investment in affordable rental housing in the Netherlands is severely limited due to weak financial viability. This issue is compounded by higher interest rates, unfavorable fiscal changes, and stringent rental regulations, making it more attractive for investors to sell existing rental properties on the owner-occupied market rather than continue leasing them. Consequently, foreign investors have largely exited the market, leaving domestic investors to drive demand, albeit with caution.
viewpoints.source_title: Recovery in Dutch commercial real estate is less robust than it appears

viewpoints.title: Sustainability efforts in Dutch HOAs undervalued due to lack of transparency
viewpoints.description: The value of sustainability preparation efforts in Dutch Homeowners' Associations (HOAs) is largely invisible to prospective buyers, leading to weak investment incentives. Despite evidence that energy label improvements increase property values by 2-10%, this progress is not reflected in prices because buyers lack insight into HOA's preparatory phases. This transparency gap, coupled with financial constraints and diverging interests among members, postpones collective sustainability measures, hindering overall renovation pace.
viewpoints.source_title: The hidden value of sustainability efforts in Dutch HOAs

viewpoints.title: Airbnb compounds Belgian housing pressure, but structural issues are key
viewpoints.description: Short-term rental platforms like Airbnb contribute to housing market pressures in Belgium by removing approximately 5,000 homes from the regular housing supply in major cities, representing about 0.8% of the rental stock. While significant, this is only a part of the broader housing affordability challenge. Structural bottlenecks, including historically low construction activity, a mismatch between new supply and demand (e.g., declining apartment permits despite rising demand), and escalating construction and financing costs, remain the primary drivers of housing market tightness.
viewpoints.source_title: Airbnb only part of Belgium’s housing affordability problem

demand_drivers.description: Despite headwinds, the EU economy has shown surprising resilience, which generally supports construction activity, albeit with a lag.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecasted year-on-year growth for EU construction output, which includes residential building activity. Follows a 1.8% decline in 2024 and 2.3% growth in 2025.
market_sizing.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

demand_drivers.description: Number of permits issued for new houses is a key indicator of future residential sector volumes, typically translating to home completions within one to two years.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of the trend in the number of building permits issued for new dwellings in the EU. Permits rose by approximately 15% between summer 2024 and end 2025, then broadly stabilized, indicating fading momentum.
market_sizing.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

demand_drivers.description: Post-pandemic rebound in housing demand supported a sharp rise in building permits.

market_sizing.methodology: Observation of Spanish housing permits, which nearly tripled between 2019 and 2024, reflecting a rebound from a low pre-pandemic base. Momentum has eased, with permits falling by almost 2% in Q2 2026.
market_sizing.source_title: Europe's construction sector faces a period of weak growth

demand_drivers.description: Strongest momentum in permit activity is driven by new residential construction, reflecting improving conditions for developers.
Growing share of apartment permits aligns with demographic changes and demand for smaller units, particularly in urban areas.

market_sizing.methodology: Observed year-on-year growth in Belgian building permits for H1 2026. Overall permits +8% YoY, new construction +12% YoY, residential renovation +6% YoY, residential new construction +14% YoY. July housing permits jumped +51% MoM, lifting annual growth to +11%, with apartment permits +8% YoY and house permits +14% YoY.
market_sizing.source_title: Belgian building permit recovery continues, but challenges lie ahead

demand_drivers.description: Demand for energy-efficient homes remains resilient, driven by financial benefits from reduced energy expenses, stricter renovation standards, and hedging against future energy price shocks.

market_sizing.methodology: Observed quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year changes in Belgian housing transactions and prices for Q2 2026, alongside forecasts for nominal median house price growth. Transactions increased by 2.4% QoQ, but were 4.1% lower YoY. House prices rose 0.2% QoQ and 5.3% YoY. Nominal median house prices are forecast to increase by 2.5% in 2026 and 2.0% in 2027.
market_sizing.source_title: Second-quarter resilience masks a more challenging outlook for Belgian housing

demand_drivers.description: An increase in issued building permits is expected to gradually translate into more housing construction, supporting a modest recovery in new home supply.

market_sizing.methodology: Number of building permits issued for new-build homes in the Netherlands in May 2026, marking the highest monthly number since 2015. Forecasted new-build home completions are 71,000 for 2026 and 74,000 for 2027.
market_sizing.source_title: Dutch housing permits hit 10-year high, but construction still slow off the…

demand_drivers.description: More homes coming onto the market, including former rental properties, are boosting transactions by giving buyers more choice and improving market mobility.
Expected wage growth (around 3% YoY) continues to support consumer purchasing power, bolstering demand for owner-occupied homes.
First-time buyers are bringing more of their own funds and receiving increasing support from municipalities through loans, easing access to homeownership.

pnl_drivers.description: Larger supply, higher mortgage rates, and weaker consumer sentiment are reducing upward pressure on house prices. Price growth is expected to be 3% in 2026 and 1.5% in 2027.

market_sizing.methodology: Forecasted number of existing home sales in the Netherlands for 2026, increasing from 239,000 in 2025, surpassing the previous record of 242,000 in 2017. Sales are expected to edge down slightly to 240,000 in 2027.
market_sizing.source_title: More Dutch housing supply pushes transactions to record highs

pnl_drivers.description: A one-step improvement in an apartment's energy label increases its price by 2-3%, and by 9-10% for four steps, demonstrating a direct impact on property value.

market_sizing.methodology: Total number of homes within Homeowners' Associations (HOAs) at the beginning of 2024, representing approximately 19% of the total Dutch housing stock. 48% are owner-occupied, 32% private rentals, and 20% housing association properties. Roughly 67% are mixed HOAs. Over 41% of all privately rented homes are part of an HOA.
market_sizing.source_title: The hidden value of sustainability efforts in Dutch HOAs

demand_drivers.description: A decline in homeownership contributes to increased pressure on rental markets.

market_sizing.methodology: Estimated impact of short-term rental platforms, like Airbnb, removing approximately 5,000 homes from regular housing supply in Brussels, Antwerp, and Ghent combined. This equates to roughly 0.8% of the rental housing stock in these regions being unavailable for permanent occupancy. Also, Belgium's homeownership rate declined from 72.4% in 2022 to 70.9% in 2025.
market_sizing.source_title: Airbnb only part of Belgium’s housing affordability problem
